quest.title: Finale
quest.description: The calamity facing Fontaine has finally come to an end. No matter what happens, the presses won't stop churning news out. In other words, the people will learn about the truth as fast as The Steambird's staffers can write it.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x30, Mora x44000, Memory of Running Stream x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The Soil Renewed: The Spina Di Rosula Talks Post-Disaster Rebuilding." I recently visited Poisson to meet with Miss Navia, spokesperson of the Spina di Rosula, and we spoke about Poisson's present and future.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Old soil can still give birth to new bloom," Miss Navia stated. "Hope is like seeing a small cookie when you're starving late at night — you just need a little of it."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Skyship Wingalet — Boon or Bane of the Fontaine Research Institute?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The various disputes that have arisen on account of Mr. Edwin have suddenly become a shield over the Institute, with Jurieu turning out to be a once-overlooked hidden gem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: People always call the first researcher mad, but few know what to call the second. And should that latter person achieve a miracle, they would find it all the harder to find a word with which to classify him and his team...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon barely recognizes the people in the reports. Are those really Jurieu and Navia? They sound like real big shots...

choices.text: They might've been real big shots from the start...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: What do you think? Pretty enthralling, eh? The Steambird's idea was pretty simple. With the disaster just having passed, we would print a free edition packed to the margins with good news to calm people down.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: The value for these big scoops lies in their inevitable follow-ups. We'll publish further reports and go into the stories behind those people.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Edwin's assistant, Jurieu, created a true flying ship, while Navia is leading people in the reconstruction of their home... I'm sure that these stories could draw even your well-traveled eye.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The articles do make me curious about how things will play out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's curious too... Wait a minute. Didn't we watch everything happen from start to finish? What's there to be curious about?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: And that's exactly why I'd like you to come conduct interviews with me. You're the best incubators of news, if you haven't noticed — and also, with you around, I'm sure I'll get to see that Duke.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you sure? Hasn't he turned you down several times already?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Oh, this time will be different. Come on! Let's head to Poisson first, and then make a trip to the Fortress. There are some things you'll only know when you get there.

choices.text: We just didn't meet them in that capacity.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! What brings you all here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! We're just having a look around!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I'm here to update myself on how things are going here. Hmm? Oh, the Fatui are here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, let me introduce you. This is Mr. Gerunt Snezhevich. He represented The Knave in sending us a large amount of supplies, and is helping with our work.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Our residents are hard at work as well. Thanks to everyone, work is progressing nicely. We've lost a lot of people, but we're moving forward — that will have to be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: Hello, Miss Charlotte. I'm a big fan of yours... I especially liked that article you wrote last year about Fontaine's stray cats.

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: But if you don't mind, could you not emphasize our role too much in your report? It's not charity we're doing here. We just happened to share the same interests as the Spina.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I get where you're coming from. I'll keep it as simple as possible... Or would you be willing to feature as "friendly neighbors"?

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: That would be fine, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back, too! How are things?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: We've finished laying down the construction materials. It'll be another hour before the workers are able to go over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're here too, Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, her reputation's greatly risen after that whole duel business with Miss Furina, so she's here in Poisson to wait out the heat... Alright, alright, she really came here to help me out.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: There's too much to consider in the reconstruction of Poisson. The Spina has need of more decision-makers... and well, I do already happen to be connected to Mr. Callas.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Wait just a moment! Do you mind me asking a few questions? You know, about how you felt before the duel, about what it was like facing down a god... There's lots of exciting material there, I'd bet!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Forget it. I'm sure you can find a better theme than that, Miss Charlotte.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ugh, I see you're the same as always... Couldn't you do me a favor, for Navia's sake?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Well, if we're talking about doing things for my sake, you might as well just take a few more photos of me — or of {NICKNAME}! It's better than wasting time persuading Clorinde, at any rate.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: #Of course I will — I'm not gonna let {F#her}{M#him} off that easy. Alright! Then everyone who wants to be in the photo gather up... and smile!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did it go? Was it a good shot? Did Paimon look cute in it?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Not bad. Your addition really helped the composition of the picture... Alright, hang on a moment, let me snap a few more shots...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Charlotte takes more pictures of Poisson to the clicking of shutters, and also does some rapid-fire resident interviews...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Alright, that should do it. I'll be back here later, anyway, so let's call it a day.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You're very quick.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Speed is of the essence when it comes to the news, and freshness is the key!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Also, not to brag, but I'm pretty good at building connections. Who knows, I might eventually get that interview with you after all, Miss Clorinde.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wow, you really do have that never-say-die spirit. I'm impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I'll hazard a guess that this is how you got that interview at the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You already knew she was going?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Whoa, you're well-informed. Let me make a guess, too. I asked Sigewinne, who told Monsieur Neuvillette, and he told you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: That's a... very complete information chain.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In truth, all Monsieur Neuvillette asked me was "When did the Fortress become so friendly towards the media?"

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I told him that it was best not to speak too soon — there's no guarantee that Wriothesley will make a personal appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You're right. I've gotta treasure every moment I have with them — in which case, I'll be making a move first!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Stay safe, now! And tell me if you hear anything interesting — I'll treat you to afternoon tea in exchange!

talks.objective: Go to the Fortress of Meropide

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, guess we're here again, huh? There's a real nostalgic feeling to this place.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Looks like you've been missing us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Duke! Did you come all the way to the entrance to greet us?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Of course. I'm here to welcome you and our dear Miss Charlotte, whom our good Head Nurse recommended to me.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: It's an honor to finally meet the much rumored Duke. Thank you for consenting to my visit to the Fortress, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: No need to thank me — but that said, I shouldn't be the focus of your interview. I trust you recall our agreement?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Of course, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Alright then, this way.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hey, no need to be so nervous. I've already taken all the photos we need.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Um... Miss Charlotte... Do these pictures really need to be published on the cover of The Steambird?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It would seem that Miss Lourvine doesn't want her face to appear beside that of Mr. Jurieu, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Sir, please don't say things like that!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, but it looks like dear Mr. Jurieu denies it. Might this interview be very important to you, then?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: No! I—I just... This is my first time being interviewed, and I'm very thankful to The Steambird for...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Haha, now, I might not look it, but I did actually meet Mr. Edwin once, and I'll be honest, I enjoyed chatting with you more — you've definitely got more of that "genius" vibe going on!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: The boat that brought about a miracle, the ark that saved the people! Why, you recreated a myth back there, like an emissary of legend!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: ...Still, if I might ask, where's that flying ship now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, looks like Charlotte's trying to get herself another exclusive scoop...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I have to apologize, but that ship is presently in the bowels of our factory. I'm afraid it won't be easy for you to get a shot of it.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Really? Then in that case, could I have an interview with you to make up for that loss?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She really does know how to squeeze opportunities for all they're worth...)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You already know my answer, I'm afraid. Best you interview our Head Nurse instead — or perhaps you'd like to take another photo of this couple of researchers?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Did you really have to use the word "couple"!?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Well, then, two solo photos will do!

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Is my hair messed up? Please, someone help me have a look...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Things sure are getting pretty lively here... Uh, we've seen this kind of thing before...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Ooh, seems like everyone's here! Would any of you like to try this new drink I came up with...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, Sigewinne...

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Ah, uh — Hey, Miss Charlotte! Why don't you, ah, take some pretty photos of our Head Nurse?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm? Uh, sure! C'mon, Miss Sigewinne, over this way. Let's find a brighter spot...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, sure... Do I have to smile?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, how've things been at the Fortress?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Same old same old, as you can see. Fontaine's undergone some changes, but this place's still more or less the same.

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Other than that flying ship. It got a tad too much attention, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: That's why I decided to let the interview go through. We should direct more public opinions toward the behind-the-scenes heroes — am I right, Mr. Jurieu? Miss Lourvine?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: You're too kind, sir. I believe that you, too, should have your day in the sun — not that you would want that, which is a pity.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I'll just leave the spotlight to you two.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You walk with Wriothesley for a while and share news from above ground with him...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I see. Lots of things happened that day, huh? Anyway, regarding that Harbinger, I'm not sure you remember, but his three young followers are still waiting for his return.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He sure did win them over, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I'll tell them that there's good news and bad news — the good being that their boss seems fine, and the bad being that they must face extended sentences for abetting his escape.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, actually, what about you? Are things gonna change for you, too?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: What change can there be? The Fortress will keep chugging along, and so will my duties.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: As to what Miss Furina's departure will mean for the nation, and if our laws and governance will be transformed... We'll leave those to the folks in the overworld.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone. The photoshoot's done!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Good. In that case, let's call it a day here.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: #Thanks for your cooperation. C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's go. Till next time, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: There'll be a next time?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Maybe! Who knows? I might write a story about the underwater factory next time. Until then!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You seem curious about the Fortress.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course! Ugh, that Wriothesley... I still remember going down to the Fortress to grill him for information on my father's case. Boy, did he take me for a ride... without telling me anything, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: But he did invite you to tea, didn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Two large pots of it, in fact — it was good tea, though.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I have to agree. The tea there is very good.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, speaking of that, would you like to have some today? I mean, you've got time, right?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I'd be partial to some shortbread.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Wow, it's like we've got a menu, or something... Sure, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Good.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What flavor of biscuits would you like, Mr. Snezhevich?

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: Me? I'm fine with anything... but I would prefer chocolate, should you have it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright. Leave it to me!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I'll go over the newly-arrived supplies with you later, Mr. Snezhevich. We should be able to finish the preparatory work today.

dialogues.speaker: Gerunt Snezhevich
dialogues.text: That works great for me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh. Is it just me, or did you get a new lipstick?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I did. It was a gift from Sigewinne. Want to give it a try? I think the color would suit you, too.

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney and the others

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees them! They really are here. How did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Navia mentioned that she stayed in touch with Lyney and the others after working together. Apparently, they've been at the docks distributing these strange pockets the whole time since.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon — ah, and Miss Charlotte, too.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Would you like a Magic Pocket?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: What sort of gadget is it?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: It's a wondrous bag that can be used to carry many things. The water level has returned to normal, but if you see any of your things floating around, you can use this to carry them — or you could trick a friend into doing it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Trick a friend? Huh, I wonder which of my friends would fall for that...?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You could just make a friend like Freminet here. Isn't that right, Freminet?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Is this what you meant by "I'll help you make some more friends"...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: To be honest, that sounds pretty sweet! Could I have your contact, please?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Uhh... Oh, um... sure. Please, write down my address.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lynette sure is working hard to help Freminet socialize...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: He was the one who proposed doing this — he even wants to assist in our magic shows.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like that would suit him.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, I was planning to first introduce Pers as an assistant, and later Freminet himself. In the future, I think we can leave underwater escape magic to him, too.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That said, would anyone want to see a diver escape underwater?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, it'll work out. Every journey begins with a first step — he'll become a part of our show eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Lynette, could you come over? Miss Charlotte says she wants to take a picture of us...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #My, that Charlotte is rather perceptive. She got rid of everyone the moment she realized I had something to say to you... So. How've things been, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm doing alright.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Father" says that you did a great deal during the latest events. She's very grateful for your contributions to Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, that's alright. We were more than happy to help... So, what's she doing now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, I guess you haven't heard. Well...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: After Lady Furina left, "Father" and Monsieur Neuvillette opened negotiations, during which he gave Fontaine's Gnosis to her as a "diplomatic gift."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A "diplomatic gift"? A Gnosis?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes. I was quite surprised at first, myself. But when I thought it over, there were actually a number of things going for it...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It could have been done as an apology for the incident with Lord Childe, or as thanks for his help in tying the All-Devouring Narwhal down...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Furthermore, "Father" did also lend significant aid to Fontaine and Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's true, but this is a Gnosis we're talking about. Doesn't this seem a bit... irresponsible?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I would agree, but I've also heard that... It seems that Monsieur Neuvillette has had a significant change of heart regarding the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So there's some reason for this that only Neuvillette knows about?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I suspect you'll have to ask him about that yourself. Ah, yes, speaking of which, I did see him strolling around the entrance to the Fortress of Meropide a while back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Isn't he real busy and stuff? Paimon didn't think he'd have the time for that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But back to the topic, the Gnosis was given to The Knave, right? What about Childe?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: They say that he's returned to Snezhnaya to recover from his wounds. I hear that the recent disaster really did a number on his health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, I guess I can now call him one of my "war buddies."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true. When you think about it, we've had loads of run-ins with the Fatui. To think we'd be allied with them this time...
So shocked by such a simple switching of sides?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah! Who—!?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Father"!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Well, well, what do you know? Come to the docks to see how my children are doing, and meet the Traveler by chance. Please do not pay my accomplishments in Fontaine too much mind. I would have done them regardless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you going to... take the Gnosis back to Snezhnaya?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That is our duty as Harbingers, yes.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Don't be too preoccupied with "sides." The goal of the Fatui concerns not a single place or person, but the entire world. With such a grand goal in mind, it is inevitable that we must wear many masks.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Switching my masks is something I've always done.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will you keep to your position?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That depends on many things, no one truly knows what the future holds. What good is honesty if you can't rely on it forever?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: As for you, I very much look forward to our next collaboration. Good things cannot be achieved alone, and you've proved yourselves to be great partners.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, I just remembered something... Please help us deliver this.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: A Vision? ... Ha, alright. I'll remember to return it. Thank you for keeping it safe for him this entire time.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: And that's a wrap for me! ...Huh!? You... You're...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Greetings, Miss Journalist.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ah, um... Hello. If I'm not mistaken, there are diplomatic channels I'll need to report to to take a photo of you...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That is correct, so forgive me, but I will not be able to serve as a subject in your article. However, feel free to write as much as you'd like about our dear magicians — and our upcoming rookie talent.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I—I will!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The sea breeze is quite pleasant. I shall continue my walk while the weather remains so agreeable. Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Farewell, "Father."

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: ...She has such an intimidating presence... I didn't even dare to take a picture... Thankfully, I've already wrapped up all of my prescheduled interviews. Thank you all — this'll be more than enough for me to write about, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Don't be too nervous. Why don't you take a Magic Pocket before you go? Here, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you take one too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To move things about?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's right. Funny — I was giving out Magic Pockets when we first met, too, and what do you know? I'm doing the exact same thing right now. So many things have happened, but the Pockets are still the Pockets.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I guess this must be "life." We will all follow our own paths, and serendipity will lead you to your fated friends.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Alright then. We'll be handing out pockets in some other districts later, so we'll get going now. Have a good day, you two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you really are here, Neuvillette! Paimon didn't think you were going to have free time this hour of the day.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: "Really"? Ah, I suppose you must have met Mr. Lyney. He took the time to greet me earlier when he passed this way.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In any case, you came at a good time. I was just considering reaching out to you to set up a meeting, so I may explain some things that I haven't had the time to before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, Paimon's glad that you remembered! Thank you for keeping us on your mind, what with you being busy and all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's have it, then. How was Fontaine actually saved? That whole business is still quite the mystery to us.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. It is strange, how words can often leave a bitter taste in the mouth when it finally comes time to say them out loud.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Neuvillette sighs softly, before telling you the truth concerning what he saw that day...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Focalors deceived the Heavenly Principles, and used Furina's endless performance to save Fontaine."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... So that's what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I only saw Furina's part, myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Focalors destroyed the divine throne of the Hydro Archon and restored your power to you, transforming you into a fully-fledged elemental dragon sovereign...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon still doesn't quite get what you did to save the Fontainians from dissolving.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: For me, the "authority of the ancient dragons" refers to absolute control over the Hydro element.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Fontainians were "incomplete humans" born of Egeria's use of the power of the Primordial Sea, with constitutions similar to that of mimics...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But so long as those primordial energies remain within them, I could use the ancient dragons' authority to grant them true "blood," after the fashion in which life was first brought into being on this planet.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In other words, when I gave my verdict, Fontainians became "true humans," and thus would naturally no longer be dissolved by water from the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Focalors must have counted on you to make that decision as well... Your verdict was the key to making the prophecy appear to have come true while saving everyone.

choices.text: You could say that it was at that moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and in a manner of speaking, Focalors finally managed to fulfill the original Hydro Archon's wish to turn Oceanids into real people, too.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It seems, from your expressions, that you still have more things you wish to ask.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ask away. I will tell you the truth as I know it.

choices.text: About the initial verdict that was passed on Childe...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I have investigated his case along many avenues, and I have learned that he once fell into an unknown chasm when he was young. There, by chance, he awakened the All-Devouring Narwhal.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But, whether it be by sentiment or reason, that should not have been enough to consider him the root cause of the disaster. At most, he would have had tangential liability.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As for the judgment passed by the Oratrice during the trial...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Whether it was due to that liability by association, or Focalors deliberately using him to buy time for us on the assumption that he would be able to hold the creature off... I cannot say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess Focalors had Fontainians in mind the whole time. In the end, it was thanks to her that they finally became real humans...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, hang on a second! Paimon's suddenly got another question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Back when Fontainians hadn't yet become real humans, were the children they had also transformed Oceanids?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Life has always flowed like water. Do you recall how Fontainians would often come to the Fountain of Lucine to pray for children?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Lynette said that the Fountain is where all the waters in Fontaine converge...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In truth, even those couples did not know that such prayers were no mere custom, but instead a form of ritual...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Those Oceanids who were blessed within the spring water would later descend as new humans in the coming months.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon... sorta gets it now? Either way, seems like this ritual won't be of any further use — but it'll probably live on as a local custom!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, hang on a sec. Paimon's still got a question about the Gnosis...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When we spoke to Lyney earlier, he mentioned that your attitude towards giving away the Gnosis had clearly changed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We guessed that there might be some reason for it that only you were aware of...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Hmm. No wonder the House of the Hearth is the Fatui's intelligence division. They are certainly sharp.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: So, regarding this specific issue, I was just getting ready to share something with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What is it?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In truth, I exchanged some further words with that lady named Skirk after sending you two back to the surface. It went something like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, about that, Wriothesley said Furina has already left. What's that all about?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ah, Lady Furina... The people are only aware that her death sentence has not been carried out. She abdicated the post of Hydro Archon and left affairs related to that title to me, before leaving the opera house.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I related Focalors' words to her faithfully and completely. After hearing them, she seemed neither saddened nor comforted...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: She simply said that... she was tired, and needed to rest.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Having said that, she then packed her things and moved out of the opera house, not unlike how an ordinary person might.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Erm... But she's still got a place to stay, right?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You need not worry. I will make arrangements to ensure that she will not want for food, clothing, board, or travel.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In truth, I am... somewhat happy for her. The wear and tear on her spirit will, of course, take time to heal...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But now that she no longer has to play the role of "Focalors the Hydro Archon," she can finally lay down her burdens and lead a normal life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you, then? What are your plans, now that you've regained your full powers as the Hydro Dragon?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: After Focalors passed on, the Oratrice also ceased to function.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: This matter will directly affect our trials. After much careful consideration, I've decided to take over its role in our courts. From now on, I shall hear cases and pass verdicts by myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like you're still considering stuff from the perspective of the Iudex, huh.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As an elemental dragon, there are indeed many things that I must do. But this power, and this duty... In a manner of speaking, you could say that both were granted to me.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As such, before I attend to my other responsibilities, I must first and foremost continue to serve Fontaine as its highest judge. The duty of the Hydro Sovereign and the duty of the Iudex shall coexist within my person.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Additionally, the Hydro Archon's departure has brought about another problem... Which is that the opera house shall no longer produce Indemnitium.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. That power was derived from the peoples' faith in the Hydro Archon, wasn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. But the various meks and machines in the city are all still okay. Where are they getting their energy from?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As I am now, I have full command over Pneumousia, and it can serve as a complete substitute — another reason why I cannot quite leave Fontaine immediately.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow. This ancient dragon's authority stuff is really quite useful, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right. They say you've given it to The Knave as a "diplomatic gift," or something...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Leaving aside their intentionality, the two Fatui Harbingers have indeed done much for us during this crisis.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Their sole remaining goal in Fontaine, at least at this point, would seem to be the Gnosis.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The Oratrice has ceased to function. The Hydro Archon's divine throne is now no more. And I do not need the Gnosis's power...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As such, it has lost all meaning for Fontaine.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If the Fatui have impure designs, then we might as well accede to their request now... and avoid unnecessary conflict.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah, what complicated considerations... Paimon thought you were just giving it to them out of gratitude to The Knave, and as an apology to Childe.

choices.text: About the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You will soon be heading to Natlan, I presume?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I'm afraid that I have little talent as a travel guide, so all I can do is tell you what I know about that land.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As far as I'm aware, Natlan can be said to be "a nation of dragons."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A nation of dragons? You mean, like you?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: No, I suspect that I would not find myself welcome there.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Unlike ancient dragons such as myself, the dragons of Natlan have undergone long years of development and evolution. Large numbers of them have entered a form of coexistence with humanity.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Natlan is also the nation of "war." War ravages those lands like an undying flame.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: There is one other piece of information I got incidentally from my negotiations with The Knave that I believe may be useful to you.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...The Harbinger known as The Captain has thrown his hat into the endless ring of war.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The Captain"... Sounds like a real tough customer. Seriously, everywhere you look, there's a Fatui Harbinger doing their thing!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I suggest that you fully prepare yourself before going to Natlan. In the meantime, Fontaine's doors will always be open to you.

choices.text: That the Fontainians were finally truly "born."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Well, we're going to head topside to see what's going on. You hurry over soon as well, alright, Neuvillette...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: What next...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Hmm. The All-Devouring Narwhal isn't here, so I'm no longer getting any interference.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I can finally catch the scent of your power... what it's made of.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It is the authority of the planet's primordial dragons, but with something very similar to a god's "curse" mixed in... It's quite a novel blend.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I'm sure I've encountered something like this before. What was it again...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I do not know what you speak of.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ah, of course... How could I forget:

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You should have the "remains of the Third Descender" on your person, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Remains? I've never heard of any such thing.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Huh... According to your parlance, I believe it may be called a "Gnosis"?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Well, that much is true. After Focalors' divinity faded, she handed her Gnosis to me.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But I fear I have never heard it described in the manner that you just did.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I've been training with my Master, "The Foul," ever since I was young, and I have never returned to the surface since, so most of the information I possess, I got from him.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It is only natural for those who are greater than humanity to possess a different sort of common sense, which is why there are so many problems in our attempts to communicate with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Regardless, you should probably get rid of objects of "misfortune," to prevent any disasters from befalling you.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: To live is in itself a blessing. But once a person dies, the bonds he once had with this world shall all turn to curses.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: What do you mean by that?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: No need to fret. These are just my... personal thoughts — and my reason for no longer wishing to return to the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This Third Descender you refer to. Who are they? And when did they die?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Master never mentioned them to me. Perhaps it just wasn't that important for me to know.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: If you're interested, though, I could ask him. I'll be sure to pass the answer on to you next time.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Next time... You believe we will meet again?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I do... Wait, I have a disciple of my own, don't I? He can be the messenger, then.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...That's what she told me. Whether it would prove useful or not, I wanted to pass that information on to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The remains... of the Third Descender?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what the Gnoses actually are? Paimon just thought that they looked like chess pieces. How could they be a person's remains?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: All the same, assuming that there was no misunderstanding or special metaphor at play, that is what she meant to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And she said that it would bring "misfortune" and that you should chuck it, which is why you gave it to the Fatui...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If she speaks the truth, then I would simply be putting Fontaine at unnecessary risk by keeping it here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A Descender... She mentioned one of them...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: One, that the Gnoses are related to Descenders.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I had guessed that you might already be familiar with this concept, but I did not expect you to be one of them.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: That means that the Gnoses, which are exceedingly element-compatible and can even enhance elemental abilities, do indeed come from the Third Descender.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Hmm, I wonder... Does your body also possess similar properties?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like... Uhh, like being able to use elemental powers without a Vision? That does sorta count as special compatibility, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, let's not think about this stuff right now. It just feels creepy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Comparing {NICKNAME} to the dead Third Descender and all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I won't die so easily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's what you say, but this topic still feels like bad luck.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Once Childe recovers, let's get some more answers out of him — or go look for his Master and get the answers that way!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I, too, believe it unwise to make too many blind guesses when information is lacking. The same is true of being at court.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Whatever the case, it seems like the crisis here in Fontaine's over for now.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Yes. All of Focalors' efforts were for this moment as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... She sacrificed herself in the end as a god, and she suffered through all those years as a human... Was that really what she wanted?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...I suppose that would be the mystery of a god's will.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can you understand the will of the gods?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I suspect not. But once in a while, I too would guess that if wishes were like the clouds in the sky, they will one day return to the earth as raindrops...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Life flows like water, and rain is the final answer. The water levels may sometimes tilt one way or another, but the rain falls fairly upon all.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And what, ultimately, is the difference between the rains that fall upon all of us?

choices.text: For me, this information means two things.

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Here are the interview notes. They mention that the flying ship may have many uses in the future, and the journalist asked me what I thought of them...

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: ...Seriously, how would I know anything about that? Flight is just flight. Whether people want to use a flying ship to broadcast good news or organize weddings is none of my beeswax.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: A wedding... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Why are you looking at me like that?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: So, the flying ship can be used for weddings?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: I didn't say that. That journalist mentioned it... And what does that have to do with us, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: ...True. What does that have to do with us?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: *sigh* You know, I'd love to see you in one of Charlotte's photoshoots one day.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Is that really necessary? Our line of work doesn't really require much photographing.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: It's precisely because we don't need the pictures that they'll have value as keepsakes. You don't really look all that opposed to the idea, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Maybe I'm just happy that I managed to once again avoid the spotlight. I think this interview went well, either way.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yes, you successfully kept prying eyes away by using Mr. Jurieu and Miss Lourvine as shields. Very good.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You should be happy for them. They have a bright future ahead of them.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Alright. Last stop, the docks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The entrance to the Fortress... Ooh, he really is there!
